title: fix(sharing): defer to an app-authored RLS widener before hard-refusing a by-id write (#5493)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#5493

Step 2 of the ruled two-step chain. Step 1 (PR #6841) landed
`ISecurityService.checkAuthoredRowWrite`; this PR is its only consumer.

## The defect, restated as the mechanism

HotCRM's 17.0 GA sweep declared two RLS update-wideners on one profile and
measured one of them working. On the junction `crm_campaign_member` a non-owner
PATCH returned 200; on `crm_campaign` the identical shape returned 403
`FORBIDDEN: insufficient privileges to update crm_campaign`. That sentence is
the sharing middleware's, not the row gate's `(row-level security)` — so the
refusal landed **before** RLS was consulted and the declared widener was never
asked.

The discriminator is not "carries sharing rules" (the issue's own wording) but
**whether record sharing enforces on the object at all** (round-2 refinement,
comment 5226364929): `checkEdit` abstains — so `canEdit` answers `true` and the
write reaches RLS — when the effective sharing model is `public` (which
`controlled_by_parent` maps onto) or when the schema has no `owner_id` field. A
junction lands in that set; an ordinary owned business object does not. Same
declaration, opposite outcome, split by a property no author writes down.

Premise re-verified on `origin/main` before implementing: the mechanism holds,
but the triage anchor's line number has drifted — the throw is now at
`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts:913` (was :857), after
plugin-sharing absorbed #6552.

## Conclusion per authority face

**1. Sharing middleware — CHANGED, in the refusal branch only.**
`buildSharingMiddleware`'s by-id write gate no longer ends the decision by
itself. When `canEdit` / `canDelete` refuse (i.e. `checkEdit` / `checkDelete`
answered `deny`), it asks `service.probeAuthoredRowWrite(object, id, verb, ctx)`
before throwing. `admit` retracts THIS authority's refusal and calls `next()`.
Every other outcome falls through to the existing throw, byte for byte —
including the ADR-0111 D10 delete-denial breadcrumb, which still fires on every
refusal that survives. The builder's signature is unchanged: the probe rides the
`security` late-binding the passed `SharingService` already holds for
`hasWriteBypass`, so no caller changes and no runtime dependency on
`@objectstack/plugin-security` is introduced (the dependency still runs the
other way).

**2. Security pre-image gate — UNTOUCHED, and still correct after the deferral.**
No production file in `plugin-security` is modified. The deferral does not
authorize anything: it removes one of two independent refusals and hands the row
to the pre-image gate, which composes per #6684 / #5492 and makes the final row
decision. So the composite is strictly the intersection it always was, minus the
one term the ruling declared wrong. Concretely, in the flipped control the
security gate is what admits `opp_theirs` (the app policy `stage ==
'prospecting'` OR-combining past the platform ownership floor) — if it had
refused, the write would still be refused with the `(row-level security)`
envelope, which is exactly what the guards on `crm_note` and `READ_SHARE_CTX`
in that file keep measuring, green and verbatim.

**3. `checkAuthoredRowWrite` consumption — fail-closed, absence == `abstain`.**
`SharingSecurityProbe` gains the method as an OPTIONAL structural member, and
`SharingService.probeAuthoredRowWrite` is a passthrough with no logic of its own
to drift. It returns `abstain` — the direction that changes nothing, because the
caller uses `admit` to widen — for: no `security` service at all, a late-bound
lookup that throws, a service predating the method (feature-detected with
`typeof`), a probe that throws (logged, never rethrown), a principal-less
context, an on-behalf-of context (ADR-0090 D10 — the delegator intersection is
composed by the middleware, which gates twice, so one verdict cannot stand for
both identities), and any verdict that is not the literal string `admit`. The
last two are the consumer's OWN guards rather than properties borrowed from the
reference implementation, because this plugin late-binds structurally to
whatever is registered as `security`.

Deliberately NOT done: nothing feeds `checkEdit` / `checkDelete` /
`buildWriteFilter`. Folding the probe into the sharing verdict would make the
two authorities read each other in a circle, since #5492's composition reads
that verdict off this service.

**4. The flipped control — substantively flipped, not deleted.**
`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/row-write-widener-composition.test.ts`
carried a dedicated #5493 control asserting the OLD position. It now asserts the
deferral, and the load it carries is the same load:
`sharing.checkEdit(...)` is still pinned to `deny` (nothing widened the sharing
verdict), `security.checkAuthoredRowWrite(...)` is pinned to `admit` (the
predicate is the service's, not this middleware's — ruling Q1 = A), the write
succeeds, and `next_step` is asserted to have really become `updated`. A
completed write over an unchanged row would mean the chain was bypassed, not
that the fix works. Only that one case is touched; the ten #5492 guards in the
file are verbatim and green.

**5. The E-A guard — pinned on the sharing side too, not delegated to step 1.**
The platform's ownership floor (`created_by == current_user.id`, shipped on the
additive `member_default` baseline) matches a record transferred away from its
creator, so a deferral keyed on "the composed RLS admits this row" would hand
transferred records back to former creators. `crm_campaign` fixture
`camp_transferred` is that shape, and the new suite pins it three ways: the
fixture really is E-A (floor matches, ownership moved, the principal's own
authored widener names a stage this row is not in), the write stays refused with
the full ADR-0112 envelope, and the probe was CALLED and answered `abstain` — so
the refusal is the abstention holding, not the deferral never running. The same
principal IS admitted on a row their policy really names, which pins that the
guard is the row, not the person.

## Scope held

- **Bulk is out of scope (#6736).** The deferral is in the by-id branch only
  (ruling Q2 = A1, verdict-shaped, by-id only). A case drives the middleware's
  bulk branch and pins that the AST is still scoped by ownership, unwidened, and
  that no verdict is asked.
- **#6698's boundary is unaffected** — measured, one sentence: on an object with
  no `owner_id` field `checkEdit` abstains, `canEdit` answers `true`, the gate
  never enters the refusal branch, so the probe is never reached and the
  platform `created_by` floor remains that object's only row-level write gate.
  Pinned as `calls` being empty on `crm_note`.
- No `packages/spec` changes, no `plugin-security` production changes, no
  `content/docs/releases/`.
- ADR-0111 D3 verb boundaries unchanged: an edit-share still widens update and
  not delete, and an update-only authored widener does not open delete either —
  the verb is threaded into the verdict, not collapsed onto `update`.

## Tests

New: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/authored-row-write-deferral.test.ts`
(20 cases) — real `SharingService` + real middleware + a structural `security`
stub modelling step 1's ruled semantics (authored/non-floor policies only; the
platform floor is deliberately absent from the fixture, which is the whole point
of E-A). `plugin-sharing` cannot depend on `plugin-security` (the dependency runs
the other way), so the REAL service driving the REAL composition is measured
end-to-end by the flipped control in `plugin-security` instead. Every
rejection-class case asserts `code` AND `status` plus the message's first
sentence; there is no bare `toThrow()`. The new fake engine opens `update` with
`assertEngineUpdateDispatch` and `delete` with `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`.

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test
  plugin-sharing   Test Files 15 passed (15)   Tests 396 passed (396)
  plugin-security  Test Files 42 passed (42)   Tests 861 passed (861)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck  -> Done
```

## Reverse verification — direction predicted before running

Mutation: `git checkout origin/main -- .../sharing-plugin.ts` (removes ONLY the
middleware deferral; the service passthrough and every test stay), then
`plugin-sharing` rebuilt so `plugin-security` consumes the mutated `dist`.

Predicted **red**: the two admit-cases and the flipped control, with the
`FORBIDDEN` signature. Measured: **6 red in plugin-sharing + 1 red in
plugin-security**, and the prediction was one short — reported as measured
rather than tidied.

- Fully red, FORBIDDEN signature, as predicted: the HotCRM-shape PATCH, "the
  same creator IS admitted on a row their policy names", and the flipped
  control (`AssertionError: FORBIDDEN: insufficient privileges to update
  crm_opportunity opp_theirs: expected { ok: false, code: 'FORBIDDEN', … } to
  match object { ok: true }`).
- Red only on their EVIDENCE half, exactly as predicted — their guard half
  stayed green because the refusal is what `main` already does: the E-A case
  (`expected [] to have a length of 1`) and the delete verb-boundary case
  (`expected [] to deeply equal [ { object: 'crm_campaign', … } ]`).
- **Not predicted, same shape:** "a probe that THROWS" went red on
  `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with …` — with the deferral gone the probe is
  never invoked, so the throw never happens and the abstention breadcrumb is
  never logged. Its refusal assertions stayed green. I had counted this case as
  a pure guard; it also carries evidence, and the evidence moved.
- **Stayed green, and correctly so:** all ten #5492 guards, and in the new suite
  the no-widener refusal, the owner's own write, both share cases, the junction
  passthrough, #6698, the five remaining fail-closed cases, on-behalf-of,
  principal-less, and bulk (14 of 20). Every one of them asserts a refusal plus
  an empty `calls`, and removing the deferral produces exactly that — a guard
  that stays green under its own author's mutation is the guard working, not a
  test that failed to bite.
- In the flipped control, `checkAuthoredRowWrite` still resolved `admit` under
  the mutation, which isolates the loss to the deferral rather than to step 1's
  verdict.

Restored, rebuilt, re-run: 396 + 861 green.

## Gates

`.github/workflows/lint.yml`'s ESLint job enumerated and run one by one — all 33
green (`lint`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:query-options-erasure`,
`check:verify-stand-in`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-authoring`,
`check:docs-audit-scope`, `check:role-word`, `check:quick-reference-counts`,
`check:adr-anchors`, `check:org-identifier`, `check:authz-resolver`,
`check:service-providers`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:error-code-casing`,
`check:wildcard-fallthrough`, `check:meta-type-normalized`,
`check:init-service-contract`, `check:durability-log-level`,
`check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:objectui-changeset`,
`check:release-notes`, `check:release-body`, `check:node-version`,
`check:workflow-status-functions`, `check:shard-attestation`,
`check:published-files`, `check:engine-double-contract`,
`check:kernel-hook-pairs`, `check:resume-authority-declared`,
`check:driver-memory-census`, `check:merge-driver`, `check:spec-parsed-alias`).
Plus the TypeScript job: full workspace `turbo run build` (70/70) and
`turbo run typecheck` (120/120), `check:type-check-coverage`,
`check:type-check-debt`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`,
`check:app-nav-i18n`; and from the other workflows
`check:override-consistency`, `check:console-sha`. `check-adr-0087-registration`
(pr-automation.yml) fires on breaking changesets — this changeset is `patch`.

Changeset: `.changeset/sharing-defer-authored-row-write-widener.md`
(`@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch`).
